newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says to meet all securities obligations.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says to meet all securities obligations.

text.p: Germany will honour all its securities obligations even if it decides on some delay on repayments of old east German or railway debt, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.

Responding to a comment by CDU parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble that the Bonn coalition was considering such a delay, to help solve its budget crisis, the ministry said it would not affect publicly traded debt, only debt held by government agencies.
"The federal government will meet all its obligations," a Finance Ministry spokeswoman told journalists.
The coalition is merely considering adjusting the level of annual repayment, the spokeswoman said, without going into detail.
Germany, struggling like other European nations to rein in its budget deficit this year to qualify for European monetary union, is having to resort to far-reaching measures.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel is due to submit his 1998 budget to the cabinet next week.
